newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: NPF CHIEF SAYS NOMURA FAVOURITE IN TENDER.
newsitem.headline: NPF CHIEF SAYS NOMURA FAVOURITE IN TENDER.

text.p: Japanese investment bank Nomura is seen as the front runner to take a 31.5 percent stake in the fourth largest Czech bank IPB a.s., the chairman of the Czech National Property Fund (NPF) was quoted as saying.

Roman Ceska, the head of the NPF, a state privatisation agency, said in an interview with the daily Pravo on Monday that the tender process for the sale of the state's stake in IPB would probably take about six months.
"I believe that Nomura will confirm its interest in IPB and that it will emerge as the (potential) partner with the biggest chance of getting into this bank," Ceska was quoted as saying.
Apart from Nomura, ING Groep NV and ABN AMRO have also been touted by the Czech media as parties interested in taking a stake in IPB although both have refused to comment on the matter.
Ceska also said it was high time that the Czech Republic firmed up its plans to privatise shares in its biggest banks.
He added however that the sale of shares in these banks would not begin for "two or three years".
The Czech state retains large stakes, held by the NPF, in its four largest banks - IPB, Komercni Banka , Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna .
